title: Bright Angel biota of the Grand Canyon
summary: About 505 million years ago, in a shallow Cambrian sea, the sediments of the Bright Angel Formation in what is now the Grand Canyon buried trilobites, brachiopods and trace fossils. A 2025 study added exceptionally preserved small fossils of priapulid worms, crustaceans and molluscs.

uncertainty.note: The 2025 paper gives the formation as middle Cambrian, about 507 to 502 million years old, and about 505 Ma in its introduction; the National Park Service gives the wider Tonto Group as roughly 510 to 500 million years.

as_recorded.value: Tonto Group deposited between about 510 and 500 million years ago

where.modern_name: Grand Canyon, Arizona, USA (fossils from the central canyon, Bright Angel Formation)
where.historical_name: Shallow marine shelf near the Shinumo archipelago on the Laurentian margin (no polities)

paleo.note: Modern Grand Canyon point reconstructed to 505 Ma; the PALEOMAP model gives 0.07, -95.12 for the same point, so the models differ.

importance.justification: A regional Cambrian fauna that shows life on an oxygenated shelf beside better-known sites like the Burgess Shale.
